citation: Kaslow et al. (2016), Developing a CubeSat Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) Reference Model - Interim Status #2
title: Developing a CubeSat Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) Reference Model - Interim Status #2
venue_type: conference paper, IEEE/AERO proceedings; paper text shows IEEE copyright, but the exact venue heading is not printed in the converted text
modeling_scope: System-level CubeSat MBSE reference model in SysML/OOSEM covering stakeholders, needs, objectives, constraints, measures of effectiveness, requirements, logical mission enterprise architecture, logical space and ground subsystems including the power subsystem, subsystem-level power and weight parametrics, data/information flows, operations phases, lifecycle framing, concept trade studies, COTS simulation-tool interfaces, and general validation/verification strategies.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML with Object-Oriented Systems Engineering Method (OOSEM); No Magic/MagicDraw graphical modeling tools; COTS modeling and simulation tool interfaces; model distribution mechanisms considered include MagicDraw, ZIP, XMI, OpenMBEE, and Teamcenter.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite reference platform; generic CubeSat unit/form-factor discussion with mission-specific CubeSat models; prior phases applied the model to the Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX), a 3U CubeSat.
task_domain: CubeSat space mission systems engineering, reference architecture development, and concept life-cycle mission design/trade studies across space, ground, launch, communication, and mission-support elements.
interface: Reference model feeds mission-specific CubeSat models; SysML model interfaces with COTS modeling and simulation tools; distribution mechanisms include MagicDraw/ZIP/XMI/OpenMBEE/Teamcenter; domain interfaces include launch vehicle interface system, communication services, space-ground communication, and mission payload-bus adapter.
feedback: Concept trade-study process identifies parameters driving MOEs, MOPs, and TPMs and then carries out trades; distributed model context includes user feedback mechanisms; SysML model changes are automatically populated into system views.
evaluation: Interim/status demonstration through described SysML reference-model artifacts and prior RAX applications: behavior simulations, COTS simulation-tool interfaces, downlink/power trades, and energy/data trade studies. The current phase reports model structure and diagrams rather than quantitative validation; creating an example mission-specific model and validating MOEs/MOPs are next steps.
rq_relevance: RQ1: yes for a general nanosatellite/CubeSat system-level MBSE model; EPS evidence is limited to a logical Power subsystem and subsystem-level power/weight parametrics. RQ2: partial because outcomes are model integration, reuse, consistency, checklist value, trade-study support, and reduced systems-engineering burden, not explicit EPS reliability outcomes. RQ3: partial because V&V appears in the MBSE definition, Tester role, Cal Poly testing-requirements model, and mission-specific validation/verification strategies, but the paper does not specify EPS-specific verification procedures.
claimed_outcomes: Integrability: the system model helps integrate discipline-specific engineering models and simulations, and prior phases interfaced with COTS simulation tools.
Consistency/configuration: requirements and design are contained in a single authoritative integrated model, and model changes automatically populate system views.
Reproducibility/reuse: the CubeSat Reference Model is intended as a starting point adaptable to mission-specific CubeSat models.
Uniformity/checklist: a properly designed reference model is claimed to serve as a checklist and promote uniformity and consistency across future CubeSat models.
Process efficiency: MBSE is claimed to reduce the burden of systems-engineering tasks for small CubeSat teams.
Analysis support: the model provides a basis for concept life-cycle trade studies using stakeholder MOEs decomposed into MOPs and TPMs.
verification_validation_linkage: General system-level V&V linkage only. MBSE is defined as supporting verification and validation; the model includes a Tester stakeholder responsible for V&V, Cal Poly testing requirements in SysML, and mission-specific validation and verification strategies. No EPS-specific verification procedure, test sequence, or IV&V workflow is specified.
key_findings: The paper presents an interim status of an INCOSE SSWG CubeSat MBSE Reference Model intended as a generic SysML/OOSEM logical architecture for future CubeSat developers.
The current model starts from stakeholders and captures needs, objectives, constraints, measures of effectiveness, and generic CubeSat architecture down to logical subsystems.
The CubeSat mission enterprise is decomposed into space system, ground system, launch services, launch vehicle interface system, and communication services.

The logical space system includes a Power subsystem described as generating, regulating, storing, and distributing spacecraft power, and the minimum distribution model includes subsystem-level power and weight parametrics.

Prior phases applied the approach to RAX and demonstrated behavior simulation, COTS tool interfaces, and trade studies involving data rate, available power, signal-to-noise ratio, on-board energy, solar panel area, battery capacity, orbital altitude, and ground station network.
Verification is present at the general MBSE/reference-model level, but not as an EPS-specific verification procedure integrated before physical development.
Distribution and licensing are treated as part of making the reference model usable by CubeSat teams and classrooms while protecting team contributions.
limitations_gaps: The paper states that the fourth-phase modeling effort starts anew.
The effort to date has focused on nomenclature, stakeholder content, measures, and generic architecture down to logical subsystems; an example mission-specific model remains future work.
Validation of MOEs and MOPs is identified as a next step rather than reported as complete.
Distribution, licensing, and copyright options are still being considered.
Formal threats to validity are not discussed.

quality.rationale: IEEE conference/proceedings DOI and copyright indicate a credible venue. The paper discusses interim status and future work, including missing mission-specific example and MOE/MOP validation, but does not provide a formal limitations or threats-to-validity discussion.
